_doc:
Founding households and kin (Phase 009). Figures are for a pre-industrial English village. Every figure marked APPROX is recalled from the cited source's general findings and was NOT checked against the text in this phase; verify before relying on the exact value.

HOUSEHOLD_SIZE: share of households by number of members (9 = nine or more). Shape from Laslett 1972 (Household and Family in Past Time, Cambridge UP, introduction and English tables) and Wrigley and Schofield 1981 (The Population History of England 1541-1871, ch. 4): mean household size about 4.5-4.8 (APPROX).
EXTENDED_FAMILY: share of households that contain a kinsman beyond the nuclear family. About one in ten in Laslett's English listings (APPROX).
EXTENDED_KIN: which kinsman, given an extended household. Grandparent co-residence is the commonest form Laslett recorded (APPROX split).
AGE_AT_FIRST_UNION: mean and spread of age at first marriage, England 1600-1800: women about 26, men about 27-28 (Hajnal 1965, European marriage patterns in perspective; Wrigley and Schofield 1981) (APPROX).
CHILDREN_PER_UNION: children ever born to a marriage that lasted to the wife's late child-bearing; mean about 4.5-5 (Wrigley and Schofield 1981) (APPROX).
INFANT_SURVIVAL: share of births surviving the first year, England 17th-18th centuries about 0.75-0.85 (Wrigley and Schofield 1981) (APPROX; mid of range).
ADULT_LIFESPAN: age at death of an adult, mean and spread. Life expectancy at 20 about 35-40 more years (Wrigley and Schofield 1981) (APPROX).
PARENT_AGE_AT_BIRTH: parent's age at a child's birth; mothers mostly 20-40 (APPROX; Wrigley and Schofield 1981 fertility tables).
KIN_MODEL: model parameters of the founding genealogy (not measured facts): SIBLING_MAX_GAP_YEARS is the widest age gap between a household head and a sibling who may live in the same household (about two years between births times about seven births per sibship; APPROX). GRANDPARENT_REUSE is the chance that a parent's parents are a couple already in the record (so two parents are siblings and their children are cousins); SPOUSE_IN_VILLAGE is the chance a married founder's spouse is another founder. EVER_MARRIED is the chance a founder has a union. CHILD_SPACING_YEARS caps a couple's children in a short window (birth interval in pre-industrial marriages about two years, Wrigley and Schofield 1981) (APPROX). All APPROX.
KINSHIP_STREAM: the random stream offset from the map seed used for the founding genealogy, so it never shares the world's draws.
HOUSEHOLD_TARGETS: the cited value each self-test sample is checked against, with the tolerance. Failing a tolerance is an error.

Checked 2026-11-05 (supervisor): mean household size about 4.75 in England from the sixteenth century to 1911 is Laslett's figure (P. Laslett, 'Size and structure of the household in England over three centuries', Population Studies 23 (1969) 199-223; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22077606/). Relatives beyond unmarried children in about 11 per cent of pre-industrial English households (summary of Laslett's 100-community sample: https://www.encyclopedia.com/history/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/households). The other figures remain APPROX.

mean_size.source: Laslett 1969 (Population Studies 23) and Laslett 1972, 4.75; Wrigley and Schofield 1981

extended_share.source: Laslett 1972, about 10-11% of households with kin
